stem: An added protocol writes X, Y and Z separately while the controller may read between writes. Which design best prevents execution of a pose mixing different observations?

options.text: Acknowledge each coordinate write separately while allowing the controller to execute as soon as it reads X.
Finish an immutable staged X/Y/Z record with a sequence identifier, atomically publish its identifier, and wait for acknowledgement before reusing its storage.
Write a new sequence number before X/Y/Z, then let the controller read that number only once and trust the following fields.
Send X/Y/Z in one transport message, then let the controller update and read the individual variables independently without a record-level commit.

assumptions: Added concurrency model, not the implementation of the omitted robosync.src. Individual scalar reads/writes are atomic, but arbitrary interleavings are possible; no implicit atomic multi-field update or bounded scheduling gap is assumed.

A staged record can be kept immutable until acknowledgement, and publishing its record identifier can be implemented atomically under the proposed correct protocol. No actual network/controller writes.
